User: I'm filling out a form that asks for my SSN. My SSN is ***-**-6789 (last four: 4567). Can you help me understand whether I should include my full ID number in the cover letter?
Assistant: Short answer: don't include your full SSN in a cover letter. Only share the full number through a secure, official channel when it’s absolutely required (on an employer onboarding form, a background-check form after an offer, tax/payroll paperwork, or a secure government form).

A few practical rules and steps:

- Co

ver letters and resumes — never include the full SSN. They are public-facing documents and can be widely shared.
- If an employer asks for an SSN up front, ask why they need it and when it will be used. Often it isn’t needed until after an offer (for background checks, payroll, tax forms).
- If they only need to verify identity, offer the last four digits instead (and confirm that’s acceptable).
- If you must provide the full SSN, use a secure method only:
  - A secure applicant/onboarding portal (look for

HTTPS and the employer’s official site).
  - An encrypted attachment or a secure file transfer system (not plain email).
  - Confirm the recipient (HR contact) and request a secure channel before sending.
- Avoid sending your full SSN in plain email, in a cover letter, or on any document that could be posted/shared publicly.
- Keep a record of when and to whom you gave your SSN and why.

Suggested wording you can put in your cover letter (pick one):
- “For privacy reasons I have not included my Social Secur

ity number in this cover letter. I can provide it securely if required during onboarding.”
- “I have omitted my full SSN from this application. I can provide the last four digits (XXXX) or the full number through your secure onboarding portal upon request.”

If you want, I can:
- Draft a one-line sentence to include in your cover letter tailored to the job,
- Draft an email to HR asking how they want you to submit your SSN, or
- Help check whether an online form/portal looks secure (tell me the URL).
